transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Well… it’s this memorial I’ve been putting together for my brother. It started small, but I guess it’s gotten bigger than I meant. I’ve been spending most days calling people, finding songs, planning displays… even trips. My wife says I’ve let the garden and my walking group and most everything else slide.
Have you been needing less sleep than usual lately?
I don’t know… I haven’t really been keeping track. Some nights are shorter, I guess, but I’m not sure if it’s more than usual.
Lately, have you been feeling unusually upbeat or energized compared with your normal self?

Yeah… I guess so. Some days I feel sort of lit up, like this memorial has to happen and people are finally going to see what my family’s been through. But then if my wife or someone at the senior center questions it, I can get… short with them. More than I should.
Have you been talking much more than usual lately?

Maybe. At the senior center, when we talk about the memorial, I’ll start explaining the songs, the quilts, the photos… and I guess I don’t stop quick enough. I’ve talked over people. My pastor had to say, real gentle, “Aaron, let’s let someone else speak.”
Have you been feeling like you have a special mission or ability that other people don’t fully understand?

I… maybe. I don’t like saying it that way.

It’s just, those old ballads my brother kept… they’re not just songs. There are warnings in them, for me. My wife says I’m reading too much into it, but I know what I heard in those words.
When you say the songs had warnings in them for you, did you actually hear a voice speaking directly to you?

Sometimes… yeah. When I’m at the kitchen table going through his song sheets, I’ll hear my brother. Like he’s behind me humming, or saying which tune comes next.

Nobody else hears it, though.
Do these experiences of hearing your brother feel to you like a comforting sense that he’s still nearby, or more like a real voice speaking out loud to you?

It’s… it’s more like a real voice, I guess.

When I’m sitting there with his song sheets, I hear him clear as day sometimes—humming behind me, or telling me which tune comes next. But nobody else in the house hears anything.
Do you believe your brother is sending you a special message meant specifically for you?

Yes… I think so.

I know it sounds odd, but those ballads weren’t just songs to him. There are warnings tucked in there, meant for me. My wife says I’m reading too much into it, but… I know what I heard in the words.
Have these experiences led to you being hospitalized, or caused major problems in your day-to-day life?

Not hospitalized, no.

But… it has caused trouble. I’ve stopped going to my walking group and book club much. The garden’s gone downhill. I’ve upset people at the senior center because I keep bringing it back to the memorial display.

My wife says most days end up being about calming me down or stopping me from making another call or trip or argument. I suppose she’s not wrong.
About how long have you been feeling this unusually energized and preoccupied with the memorial?
About two months, I suppose… since my brother passed and I started working on the tribute.
During this time, have these changes made it hard for you to manage your normal responsibilities?

Yes… I guess it has.

I haven’t kept up with things like I used to. I’ve missed my walking group and book club, and the garden’s been neglected. At the senior center, I’ve upset a few people because I keep bringing everything back to the memorial.

My wife says most days end up being about settling me down or stopping me from making another call or going somewhere about it. She’s probably right.
During the past two months, have you had a period where you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?
I don’t know… I wouldn’t say that, no. I’ve been upset at times, sure, but not depressed most of the day every day.
Have you had times when you felt so energized or driven that your wife or anyone else thought you needed urgent psychiatric help?

I don’t know about “urgent help.” My wife has been worried, yes.

I just… I can’t sit in my chair like I used to. I’m up moving boxes, making calls, sorting papers, walking room to room. Feels like I’ve got more steam in me than I ought to at my age.
Before your brother died, had you ever had a time like this?

No… not like this.

Before my brother passed, I wasn’t hearing his voice in the house or thinking songs were warning me personally. That all seemed to start when I got caught up in the memorial plans and had all this energy going.
Have you heard your brother’s voice at times when you were not feeling especially energized or driven?
No… I don’t think so. It all started around when I got swept up in the memorial work, with all that energy and planning. Before that, I never heard him in the house like that.
Have you believed that the songs contain special warnings meant specifically for you?

Yes… I have.

I know it sounds strange, but those old ballads my brother had… they don’t feel like just songs to me. There are warnings in the words, meant for me. My wife says I’m reading too much into it, but… I know what I heard.
